item.title: AEA invites the public to attend workshops on chronic condition management
item.description: LIHUE — The Agency on Elderly Affairs invites the public to take part in the Better Choices, Better Health workshop series, a no-cost six-week program beginning Feb. 23.

item.title: EDITORIAL: Up-front payments benefit nonprofits
item.description: Hawaii’s nonprofits work for the community, often on behalf of or in partnership with state and county governments, to house and care for homeless, deliver food to struggling families, assist domestic violence victims, provide health services to the underserved — the list goes on. Post-COVID, and after a particularly painful year of federal cutbacks, it is these groups that now need a helping hand.

item.title: Hawaii could see new holiday, 2 days of observance
item.description: Hawaii could see a new official state holiday marking each Lunar New Year in February and two unofficial days of “observance” to celebrate Hawaii’s libraries and honor Joseph Dutton, who followed Hawaii’s first Catholic saint in treating Hanson’s disease patients on Molokai’s remote Kalaupapa peninsula.

item.title: Kawakami condemns swastikas on hiking trail
item.description: Kauai’s mayor and police chief responded Wednesday to swastikas spray-painted along a popular hiking trail this weekend.

item.title: Trades scholarships welcomed
item.description: LIHUE — Four Kauai Community College students recently received Trades scholarships from Becky Fries of the Rotary Club of Poipu Beach.

item.title: Gabbard’s presence at election facility raid questioned

item.title: INTO LIGHT opens Sunday
item.description: LIHUE — Everyone is invited to the opening reception of INTO LIGHT Project Hawaii exhibition, Drug Addiction: Real People, Real Stories, on Sunday from 1 to 2:30 p.m. at the Kauai Community College Performing Arts Center lobby.

item.title: Trump, Dems avert shutdown
item.description: WASHINGTON, D.C. — President Donald Trump on Thursday endorsed a spending deal negotiated by U.S. Senate Republicans and Democrats that would stave off a government shutdown while lawmakers continue negotiating guardrails to rein in immigration agents, though he acknowledged a shutdown could still occur. “It could happen,” Trump told reporters. “I don’t know.” It was unclear whether the House of Representatives would embrace the deal or when it would take up the measure. item.title: Missing man identified; search continues Friday
item.description: KILAUEA — The search for a missing fisherman at Kahili Beach in Kilauea continued through sundown Thursday. First responders indicated they would resume at first light today.

item.title: High Surf Warning in effect for Kauai and Niihau
item.description: LIHUE — The National Weather Service has issued a High Surf Warning for north- and west-facing shores of Kauai and Niihau currently in effect through 6 p.m. today. The warning may be extended, dropped or modified as conditions develop.
